Muse · reference board v2

Looks like an AI product, reads like plain English.

Round 2, after Antoine's note: Clippable is a tool, not an agency, so it should look like a modern San Francisco AI product. Simple, direct, no abstract words, and it has to show many streamers being clipped live at the same time. Six new references, three new directions, and one built hero mock. The loop every direction lands in five seconds:

Pick streamers→Auto-clips→Download→Post

My pick: Live Board

The hero is the product, running. I built a static mock of it so you can judge the feel: open the Live Board hero mock. Streamer names and clips in it are placeholders. “Type a Name” (2) is the bolder idea, and I'd keep it as a later addition once there's a real demo to back it.

Round 2: how AI products show it

What these share is plain words, the real product on screen, and a visible list of things working at once.

Many things at onceScreenshot, 26 Nov 2026

Cursor

Take: One plain headline, two buttons, then the real app: a list of agents all working in parallel, each with a status. This is how to show many streamers being clipped at once.

Copy the structure: a named list with live status next to the result. Leave the warm beige.

Two-path switchScreenshot, 26 Nov 2026

ElevenLabs

Take: Three tabs sit right above the product visuals and swap the panel beneath. The cleanest split choice I found.

Use the pattern for I clip / I stream: tabs in the hero, the product panel changes. The soft orbs and cream are theirs.

Clips as the visualScreenshot, 26 Nov 2026

HeyGen

Take: A row of vertical video cards runs under a plain claim with a time in it: “made in minutes.” The visual is the output, not a diagram.

A rail of vertical clips tells our story at a glance. Same idea, with “in seconds.”

The level of directness to hit. Our UI should be the scene, not a stock backdrop.

Gumloop

Take: A big plain headline, then an actual app window with a named list of agents, connectors and status. It looks like something you could log into today.

Our streamer list with LIVE badges should read just as real.

What the board says about the category

  • Nobody makes the Clipper / Streamer split a first-class choice. Cutline hides it in the nav, ClipMe in a menu. Own it.
  • Competitors show detection (a stream, chat, a “clipped” stamp). Nobody shows the full loop through to posting. That's the opening.
  • The current staging look, a glowing globe on navy, is the generic “AI SaaS” hero. What makes ours ownable is the live streamer list plus the vertical clips, which no competitor shows together.

Three directions

These replace the first three directions (Control Room, Highlight Reel, The Engine). All of them use the brand as set. Copy rule for every one: say what it does in plain words, no “revolutionary”, no “moments”.

1

Live Board

Recommended

The hero is the product itself, running. Six streamers are live, clips drop in as they happen, and you can download each one.

Hero
Headline: “Clips from every stream, the second they happen.” Under it, one sentence: pick your streamers, Clippable clips all of them live at the same time, you download and post. Then a real-looking app window: a streamer list on the left with LIVE badges and clip counts, a feed of vertical clips on the right, a “clips in the last hour” counter and a download button on each clip. New clips slide in on a loop.
Two paths
ElevenLabs-style tabs, “I clip / I stream”, sit right above the headline. Switching them changes the headline, the app window and the sign-up button. Clippers see clips and earnings. Streamers see their own stream being clipped and who is posting it.
Look
Midnight navy, a soft blue glow at the top, the blue gradient on one headline phrase and the primary button. Geist throughout, tight and large. Mono only for numbers and timestamps. It's built, and you can see it in the mock.
Built from
Cursor, Gumloop, Linear, ElevenLabs, Cofounder's toasts
Risk
Dark blue software can look alike. The clip tiles and live list carry the identity, so they need to be well made and use real clips as soon as we're allowed to.
2

Type a Name

Boldest

Try it before you sign up. Type a streamer's name and see their latest clips straight away.

Hero
Headline: “Type a streamer. Get their clips.” One big input, as plain as Perplexity or v0. Press enter and a row of vertical clips from that streamer loads under it, with a download button on each. Below, the four steps, then the two-path tabs.
Two paths
Tabs under the input: “I clip” sends you to campaigns, “I stream” to a page about getting clipped.
Look
Same brand, but lighter: a near-white page with navy text and blue accents, the way many SF AI products open. Simple, a lot of white space, the product doing the talking.
Built from
Perplexity, v0, ClipMe's link box, HeyGen
Risk
The best conversion idea and the hardest to build. It needs a working demo with cleared streamers behind it, or it has to be faked, and we shouldn't fake it.
3

Clip Rail

Most visual

A wall of vertical clips is the hero. You know what the product makes before you read a word.

Hero
Headline: “Clips from every stream, in seconds.” A moving rail of vertical clip cards runs across the full width, each labelled with a streamer and “clipped 12s ago”. The app window sits below it.
Two paths
The same tabs as Live Board, above the rail. The rail swaps between clips (for clippers) and streamer cards (for streamers).
Look
Dark like Live Board but looser, with big imagery and less interface.
Built from
HeyGen, Medal, Whop
Risk
Needs real footage and the streamers' written permission. Until then it's coloured placeholders.

What I need before a build brief

  1. Antoine reacts to the Live Board mock: closer, or change something.
  2. The type decision. With the AI-product direction, I now recommend keeping Geist alone. It's already on the site, it's what these products use, and it keeps pages fast.
  3. For any real streamer faces, names or clips: written permission, plus a few real clips.
